paragraphs: Yosef HaBavli. (A tanna of a baraita.)

In Menachot 18a: Rabbi said, "When I went —" to Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua, "I found Yosef HaBavli sitting before him, and he was especially dear to him, up to one particular point, he said to him, 'Rabbi,' —" the face of Yosef HaBavli beamed — the eyes of (Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua, abbreviated ראב״ש) shed tears; he said, "Happy are you, Torah scholars, for whom words of Torah are especially dear," and applied to him the verse "How I love Your Torah" — and there it is implied that he also studied with Rabbi Yehuda.

And in Yevamot 74a they said: "Who is the tanna who disagrees with Rabbi Akiva? It is the tanna Rabbi Yosef HaBavli, as it was taught: Rabbi Yosef HaBavli says, etc." And in the Tosefta, Parah chapter 4: "Rabbi Yosef HaBavli says: one lacking atonement is disqualified." And in Pesachim 113b and Yoma 52b: "A tanna — he is Yosef ish Hutzal; he is Yosef HaBavli." And see the entry Isi ben Yehuda.

notes.text: Hyman abbreviates the exchange. Rashi explains עד לאחת as reaching a particular halakhah; Tosafot cites explanations meaning “exceedingly” or “as dear as one’s own life.” The rendering here follows Rashi.

The consulted Menachot 18a has Yosef’s face beaming and Elazar ben Shammua’s eyes shedding tears. Rashi’s particular-halakhah explanation and Tosafot’s exceedingly/life explanations were directly inspected; Hyman’s elisions and inferred Yehudah studentship are retained.
